questions.knowledge_point: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${f}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-\frac{y}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-y\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =-y\cdot (-\frac{2x}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{2y}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xx}(x,y)+{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =x\cdot (-\frac{2y}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}) \\  & =-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{x}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-\frac{x}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\cdot 2x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y)+{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =-\frac{2xy}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{y}^{2}-2xy-{x}^{2}}{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{y}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find ${f}_{yyx}(x,y)$ by differentiating ${f}_{yy}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{yyx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({f}_{yy}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(-{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)) \\  & =-2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-{x}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\cdot y \\  & =-2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(xy)-{x}^{2}y\operatorname{cos}⁡(xy)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing Expressions Involving Second-Order Partial Derivatives
questions.worked_solution:
To find ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y) \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)+x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+y)) \\  & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x+y)\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xx}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yy}(x,y)$ at $(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})+\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6} \\ {g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{\pi }{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3})=-\frac{\pi }{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xx}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})-{g}_{yy}(\frac{\pi }{3},\frac{\pi }{3})=\sqrt{3}-\frac{\pi }{6}-(-\frac{\pi }{6})=\sqrt{3}.
$$

First, we find the first-order derivative ${f}_{x}(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{x}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({z}^{2}{x}^{3}{y}^{2}-\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡z}) \\  & =3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{x}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xy}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({f}_{x}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}{y}^{2}{z}^{2}) \\  & =6{x}^{2}y{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ by differentiating ${f}_{xy}(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂}{∂z}({f}_{xy}(x,y,z)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(6{x}^{2}y{z}^{2}) \\  & =12{x}^{2}yz\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate ${f}_{xyz}(x,y,z)$ at $(-1,2,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{xyz}(-1,2,1) & =12(-1)^{2}(2)(1)=24\end{aligned}
$$
